title: auth/header: scoped tokens, CORS changes, request-signing nonce semantics, and OpenAI-compat alignment
author: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: This PR standardizes auth header semantics across the Redwood API and the OpenAI-compat layer. It introduces scoped project/org tokens, formalizes CORS expectations for browser-based SDKs, and adds request-signing nonce and timestamp header conventions to mitigate replay attacks. Motivation: We observed multiple interoperability issues between the Redwood hosted API and OpenAI-compat clients: ambiguous Authorization header precedence, missing project scoping, and inconsistent CORS responses that caused browser SDK failures. Additionally, security reviews recommended a lightweight nonce/timestamp signing scheme to harden public endpoints used by browser-based call patterns. Changes: 1) Introduce 'X-Redwood-Project' and 'X-Redwood-Org' optional headers; server uses them to resolve resource scoping when token is project-scoped. 2) Scoped tokens: token string prefixes now indicate scope (proj_{id}_<token> or org_{id}_<token>); server validates prefix and enforces access checks. 3) Authorization precedence rules: explicit header ordering enforced: Authorization > X-Api-Key > query param. Documentation updated to discourage query-param keys. 4) CORS: Access-Control-Expose-Headers now includes 'X-Redwood-Request-Id' and 'X-Redwood-Nonce-Required'; preflight responses now allow the new signing headers. 5) Request-signing headers: support 'X-Redwood-Nonce' and 'X-Redwood-Timestamp' for optional lightweight replay protection; servers validate timestamp skew and nonce uniqueness for a configurable window. 6) OpenAI-compat layer: map legacy 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' semantics to new scoped token rules, add compatibility translation for 'OpenAI-Organization' -> 'X-Redwood-Org' for downstream services. 7) SDKs: updates to Python and TS SDKs to surface scoped token helpers and adjust browser default CORS expectations. 8) Tests and docs: new integration tests for scoped tokens and CORS behaviour; docs/ reference pages and migration guide. Migration notes: - Existing tokens remain valid; backend accepts both legacy and scoped tokens during a transition period. - Projects should migrate to scoped tokens to enable per-project enforcement; token management UI will provide migration tooling. - Browser SDKs now set 'X-Redwood-Nonce' automatically when using the optional enableNonce flag. Testing: Unit tests added for token parsing and precedence rules; e2e tests in perf-canary emulate browser preflight with new headers. CI: security scan and runtime tests passed; one flaky e2e was retried and fixed. Rollout plan: Feature-flagged rollout across hosted regions over 2 weeks: rollout to internal orgs first, then opt-in for public tenants, then full conversion. Related: ENG-4321 design doc, PM-210 product ticket, and prior PRs pr-26001 and pr-24812 which started auth header discussions.
commits: 5 commits: 1) auth: token parser and scoped prefix validation; 2) api: CORS preflight header additions; 3) compat: OpenAI header translation layer; 4) sdk: ts/python helpers and docs; 5) tests: integration and e2e for nonce/timestamp checks.

release_notes: Authentication: introduce scoped project/org tokens and optional request-signing nonce/timestamp headers; CORS updates to expose new headers; OpenAI-compat header mapping updated. See docs/migration/auth-scoped-tokens.md for migration steps.
notes_for_ops: Ops: feature flag 'auth.scoped_tokens' controls enforcement. Default: disabled for legacy tokens; enable in controlled stages. Nonce store can be backed by Redis; default window 5 minutes. Monitor 'auth.scoped_token_rejections' metric when enabling.
